chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:

Iman is above Islam by a degree, and Taqwa is above Iman by a degree, and Al-Yaqeen is above Taqwa by a degree, and nothing has been distributed among the servants that is less [scarcely given] than Al-Yaqeen.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual hierarchy between Islam, Iman, Taqwa, and Yaqeen in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Rida (peace be upon him) delineates a four-tier spiritual hierarchy where Islam (submission) is elevated by Iman (faith), which is in turn deepened by Taqwa (God-consciousness), culminating in Yaqeen (firm conviction). This hadith from al-Kafi underscores Yaqeen as the rarest spiritual station, distinguishing it from the more common practice of Islam. In Shia scholarship, this progression reflects the journey from outward compliance to inward certainty, highlighting that true faith requires both belief and consistent piety before reaching the pinnacle of unwavering conviction.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, 
(It has been narrated) from Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The Emān is above the Islām by a level, and the piety is above the Emān by a level, and the conviction is above the piety by a level, and there has not been distributed between the servants anything more scarcely than the conviction’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn abu Nasr from al-Rida (a.s.) who has said the following:
“Belief is one degree higher than Islam. Piety is one degree higher than belief. Certainty is one degree higher above piety. Nothing is distributed among people so little as certainty is.”
